title: Off-degree vanishing of the coefficient shifted Tate constant
statement: Fix a purity finite field and coefficient setting P [def-pur-conventions, def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and a finite-type arithmetic scheme X_0 over Spec(P.field.k_0). Use the actual common-stage coefficient Weil heart [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-weil-constructible-heart] and its signed standard cohomology functors [def-sf-canonical-coefficient-weil-cohomology]. For every natural d and integer n different from -2d, coefficient H^n of twistedConstant(P,X_0,d) [lem-sf-native-coefficient-cohomology-comparison] is a zero object of the coefficient Weil heart. No smoothness, native realization or exceptional endpoint is required.

proof.text: Identify the regular completed coefficient and reconstructed integral tensor unit by fully faithful coherent reduction: both reductions identify with the same coherent system unit. Rationalize and include at the least coefficient stage to identify the common-stage units.

Compose sourceUnit, tensoring by that unit isomorphism, and the common-stage right unitor. The carrier is the root line shifted by 2d. The root line lies in the standard heart, so this carrier is both at most and at least -2d. The stage inclusion commShiftIso identifies the included shifted line with the shift of the included line.

If n<-2d, truncLE n is zero. If n>-2d, truncLE n remains at most -2d and its truncGE n is zero. Shifting preserves zero objects. Faithfulness of the heart inclusion followed by forgetting Frobenius makes each Hom to or from this object a subsingleton. The available zero arrows supply existence, hence the pair is a zero object.
